decision_record.question: What do the T03 evidence and each mandatory learner's API actually require, before any transform is written?
evidence_considered: T03-A ED-01: zero missing values across all twelve features on the full released population
docs/06 Stage 0 item 3 / frozen rule: preserve missing f0-f11 for LightGBM native handling; no imputation, no missingness-indicator feature
D17: LightGBM is the shared base-learner family for Response, T-Learner, and X-Learner

D32 (2026-08-24): the publisher's Table 2 and the official Criteo benchmark implementation define f1/f3/f4/f5/f6/f8/f9/f11 as categorical tokens, not continuous features; physical float64 storage is not evidence of semantic type
Causal Forest's exact implementation remains PROVISIONAL (ADR-CF-implementation); no estimator-specific requirement exists yet to react to
decision_record.decision: v1's no-op identity selection is SUPERSEDED by D32. X is still exactly the ordered f0-f11 columns at float64 physical storage, but LightGBM-family fitting now casts f1/f3/f4/f5/f6/f8/f9/f11 to a train-fitted pandas categorical representation (LightGBMFeatureTransform) and leaves f0/f2/f7/f10 as plain float64; this is no longer a pure identity transform for LightGBM consumers.
decision_record.why_not_more: Nothing in the current evidence requires imputation, scaling, or a missingness indicator; D32 only requires correcting feature *type* handling, not adding unrelated preprocessing.
decision_record.estimator_specific_branches: LightGBM-family stages (Response, T-Learner, X-Learner nuisance/effect) use LightGBMFeatureTransform. Causal Forest has no estimator-specific branch yet: fit_causal_forest() fails closed on the raw categorical columns pending ADR-CF-implementation's feature-representation gate (D32); it is not given a no-op pass-through.

held_out_application_rule: apply the identical train-fitted transform (continuous passthrough + train-fitted categorical vocabularies) to held-out features at T17; no refitting, no held-out-informed adjustment, unseen categories become missing deterministically

reopening_event.reason: v1's IdentityFeatureTransform treated all twelve features as generic no-op float64 columns for every consumer. This is incorrect: eight of the twelve are semantically categorical per the publisher and the official Criteo benchmark, not continuous quantities. v1 is superseded, not deleted -- its evidence remains a valid historical record of the (incorrectly-scoped) no-op transform's own internal correctness.
reopening_event.note: No new governed run has been executed under contract v2 as part of this fix. v1's T04_ACCEPTED evidence below cannot authorize v2 and cannot be reused to skip a v2 acceptance run. Any T07/T08/T09 development result that consumed v1's no-op output is STALE_FEATURE_REPRESENTATION and requires a corrected rerun under v2 before reuse.

superseded_v1_record.held_out_application_rule: apply the identical fitted (no-op) transform to held-out features at T17; no refitting, no held-out-informed adjustment
superseded_v1_record.checklist_verified: T04.1 through T04.8 (Issue #5): decision record written before implementation, no-op contract implemented and content-hashed, fit-on-train-only boundary verified against the real 9,785,714-row train / 2,096,938-row validation split, column order/dtype/determinism/missing-value-passthrough verified on real data, held-out never accessed
superseded_v1_record.note: T04 accepted independently, per Issue #5 DoD, under the (since-superseded) v1 no-op feature-semantics assumption. Retained verbatim as historical evidence; not reused to authorize v2.
